routing.method: Historical recorded-choice versus fixed fast/safe candidate sensitivity; not current-selector replay or field validation.
routing.ranking: Recorded pave + recorded unknown metres + predicted pavé probability × matched genuinely unknown metres. Never decrease uncertainty penalties or relabel as smooth. Masked test uses the same additive rule on geographically held-out labeled spans.
limitations: Only archived fast/safe geometries; no new candidate generation or legal graph validation.
Archived provider transport profiles and a maximum five-minute budget are preserved; matching also filters current modal access/direction.

Missing/incompatible provider profiles or durations are skipped; recorded profiles alone do not establish present-day legal validity. Missing/null historical budgets use the experiment's five-minute cap.
No surveyed truth for genuinely unknown roads: correct avoidance and unnecessary detours cannot be certified there.
Masked results concern mapped OSM labels, not unbiased unknown-road samples; mixed geographical OOF predictions are a sensitivity analysis, not one independent deployment model.
Unmatched/ambiguous intervals retain uncertainty; low pavé probability is never smooth-surface evidence.
Historical response surface totals can differ from current archive/matcher measurements.

limitations: OSM explicit tags, not independently surveyed truth; missing labels are not random.
Primary target is explicit cobblestone/sett; paving_stones, paved and auxiliary-only labels are excluded, not called smooth.
All highway classes included; way-level metrics are not modal or lane-kilometre accuracy.
Non-atomic source snapshots and full ways beyond source bounding boxes; experiment coverage is not runtime tile coverage.
Four large coordinate sectors are geographic holdouts, not named neighborhood boundaries or independent city replications.
No Roccella positive labels: recall and F1 undefined, city transfer unproven.
Low pavé probability is never proof of asphalt/smoothness; ensemble dispersion is not an uncertainty guarantee.
Route matching and OSM labels are partial, no physical road truth; small recorded candidate set cannot prove live routing benefit.
